quests.instruction: At the dinner table, Aarav says “Please pass the rice” and “Thank you.” His cousin grabs the dish without a word. Grabbing like that is…
quests.hint: Which behavior makes the people around you feel respected?
quests.explanation: Polite behavior shows respect for other people. Rude behavior ignores their feelings.
quests.funFact: In Japan, people often say “itadakimasu” before a meal as a polite habit.

quests.instruction: Mia broke a cup and told her dad right away. That was honest. Hiding the pieces and blaming the cat would be…
quests.hint: Honest people tell the truth, so picture the choice that needs a lie to cover it up.
quests.explanation: Honest people tell the truth, even when it’s awkward. Dishonest people don’t.
quests.funFact: In the story of Pinocchio, the puppet’s nose grows whenever he tells a lie.

quests.instruction: The line for the water slide is long. Nina waits calmly for her turn. Her brother keeps sighing and tapping his foot. He’s…
quests.hint: Picture someone sighing, tapping a foot and checking the line over and over.
quests.explanation: Patient people can wait without getting upset. Impatient people find waiting hard.
quests.funFact: “Patient” can also mean a person who is waiting for care from a doctor.

quests.instruction: At snack time, Rohan had two oranges. He gave one to a friend who’d forgotten his lunch, which was generous. Keeping both and eating them in front of his friend would be…
quests.hint: Which choice thinks only about yourself?
quests.explanation: Generous people give or share willingly. Selfish people only think about what they want.
quests.funFact: Sharing food is a big part of festivals all over the world.

quests.instruction: When Arjun finally rode his bike without training wheels, he beamed with pride. Tripping in front of the whole class and turning red would leave him feeling…
quests.hint: Think of the warm rush to your cheeks after a trip in front of everyone.
quests.explanation: Proud means feeling good about something you’ve done. Embarrassed means feeling awkward and wishing the moment would pass.
quests.funFact: When people are embarrassed, blood vessels in their face widen, which can make them blush.

quests.instruction: On the morning of the zoo trip, the children bounced with excitement. Waiting at the dentist’s with nothing to do, they just felt…
quests.hint: Time crawls when there’s nothing to play with. What feeling is that?
quests.explanation: Excited means full of eager energy about something. Bored means uninterested because nothing is happening.
quests.funFact: Scientists who study boredom think it can push people to go looking for new things to do.

quests.instruction: Before her first dance recital, Leela’s hands shook; she felt nervous. After months of practice, her older sister walked on stage feeling…
quests.hint: Who trusts that things will go well?
quests.explanation: Nervous means worried about how something will go. Confident means sure of yourself.
quests.funFact: Many people describe a fluttery feeling in the stomach when they’re nervous.

quests.instruction: On his first day at a new school, Tom stood quietly near the wall. Priya walked up to everyone, introduced herself and chatted away. Tom was shy; Priya was…
quests.hint: Picture who walks up to new people and says hello first.
quests.explanation: Shy people feel uneasy meeting others. Outgoing people enjoy it and speak up easily.
quests.funFact: Feeling shy in new places is very common, and it often fades as people get to know each other.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “like”? (cheering when pizza arrives vs. pushing the broccoli to the edge of the plate)
quests.hint: Think of how you’d treat food you push to the edge of your plate.
quests.explanation: To like something is to enjoy it. To dislike it is to not enjoy it.
quests.funFact: Tastes can change as you grow; many people start enjoying foods they once refused.

quests.instruction: Maya’s friend promised to keep a secret and always did, so Maya learned to trust her. If the friend kept telling others, Maya would begin to…
quests.hint: What happens to your belief in someone who breaks a promise?
quests.explanation: To trust is to believe someone is reliable. To doubt is to feel unsure about them.
quests.funFact: Guide dogs are trained so that people who can’t see can trust them to lead the way safely.

quests.instruction: Dev accidentally knocked over Sana’s block tower. Sana saw it was an accident. Instead of blaming him, she chose to…
quests.hint: Sana knows it was an accident. Picture how she’d reply to a sincere “sorry”.
quests.explanation: To blame is to say someone is at fault. To forgive is to let it go.
quests.funFact: “Forgive” began as an old English word meaning to give up a grudge or a debt.

quests.instruction: Two groups built bridges from paper. One shared tape and ideas and worked together. The other argued over who’d hold the scissors. The first group cooperated; the second…
quests.hint: Look for the group whose paper bridge never got started.
quests.explanation: To cooperate is to work together toward the same goal. To quarrel is to argue instead.
quests.funFact: Ants live in huge colonies, where each ant does a particular job.

quests.instruction: The sign near the pool says “No running.” Anika obeys the rule and walks. Her cousin runs anyway. He…
quests.hint: Who is breaking the rule?
quests.explanation: To obey is to follow a rule. To disobey is to break it.
quests.funFact: Pool rules say “no running” because wet floors are slippery.

quests.instruction: In the old story, the ant carries food to the nest every day without stopping, while the grasshopper plays all summer. The ant is hardworking; the grasshopper is…
quests.hint: One insect works and one plays. Who is left worrying in winter?
quests.explanation: Hardworking people put in lots of effort. Lazy people avoid effort.
quests.funFact: The tale of the ant and the grasshopper is one of Aesop’s fables.

quests.instruction: Before the exam, Jay couldn’t stop thinking about it and felt worried. His baby brother, splashing in the tub with a rubber duck, felt…
quests.hint: Picture a baby in a bath with a rubber duck: no worries there.
quests.explanation: Worried means troubled by thoughts about what might go wrong. Carefree means free of worries.
quests.funFact: Rubber toys have been made since the late 1800s.

quests.instruction: After scoring the winning goal, Karan said, “The whole team played well.” That was modest. If he kept telling everyone how amazing he was, he’d be…
quests.hint: Which kind of person talks mostly about themselves?
quests.explanation: Modest people don’t brag about what they’ve done. Boastful people can’t stop talking about it.
quests.funFact: “Modest” comes from a Latin word meaning “within limits”.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “angry”? (a person glaring at spilled juice vs. a person smiling at a perfect drawing)
quests.hint: Think of someone smiling at a perfect drawing.
quests.explanation: Angry means feeling upset and cross. Pleased means feeling satisfied and happy.
quests.funFact: Counting slowly to ten is an old trick for cooling down when you’re angry.

quests.instruction: Coach Rina told the nervous goalkeeper, “You can do this—try again!” That was encouraging. Saying, “You’ll never be any good,” would…
quests.hint: Imagine “You’ll never be any good” landing on a nervous player.
quests.explanation: To encourage is to give someone confidence and support. To discourage is to take it away.
quests.funFact: The word “courage” is hiding inside both “encourage” and “discourage”: one adds it and the other removes it.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “help”? (picking up a friend’s dropped books vs. knocking them out of his hands on purpose)
quests.hint: Which action leaves someone worse off?
quests.explanation: To help is to make things better for someone. To harm is to make things worse.
quests.funFact: “First, do no harm” is a famous principle in medicine.

quests.instruction: Asked who drew on the wall, Zubin said, “It was me.” He told the truth. If he had said, “The dog did it,” he’d have told a…
quests.hint: A dog holding a crayon? Be honest about what really happened.
quests.explanation: The truth is what really happened. A lie says something that isn’t true to fool people.
quests.funFact: Many cultures have stories about the trouble lying can cause, like “The Boy Who Cried Wolf”.

quests.instruction: The teacher gave every team the same number of points for the same mistake, which was fair. Taking more points from one team for no reason would be…
quests.hint: Check whether every team is being treated the same way.
quests.explanation: Fair means treating people equally and by the rules. Unfair means treating them differently without a good reason.
quests.funFact: Referees in sports are there to make sure games are played fairly.

quests.instruction: When the teacher asked for someone to feed the class fish, Tina’s hand shot up. Sam slowly lifted his, not wanting to do it. He was…
quests.hint: Whose hand went up slowly and with a sigh?
quests.explanation: Eager means keen to do something. Reluctant means unwilling or slow to do it.
quests.funFact: Goldfish can learn to recognize the person who feeds them.

quests.instruction: While Ravi solved the maze, he blocked everything else out and stayed focused. His friend kept looking out of the window and was…
quests.hint: Picture one boy frowning at the maze and his friend gazing out of the window.
quests.explanation: Focused means keeping your attention on one thing. Distracted means your attention keeps drifting.
quests.funFact: Switching quickly between tasks can make it harder to do any of them well.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “compliment”? (“I love your painting!” vs. “That’s the ugliest painting I’ve ever seen!”)
quests.hint: Think of a remark that would make a painter’s face fall.
quests.explanation: A compliment is a kind remark about someone. An insult is a hurtful one.
quests.funFact: “Compliment” (a kind remark) and “complement” (something that completes another) sound alike but are spelled differently.

quests.instruction: Jaya says “Good morning!” to every classmate she passes. She greets them all. Walking past with her eyes on her shoes, she’d…
quests.hint: What happens to a hello that never gets said?
quests.explanation: To greet is to welcome someone with a word or a wave. To ignore is to take no notice of them.
quests.funFact: People around the world greet each other in different ways, such as a handshake, a bow or a hand held to the forehead.

quests.instruction: Anna said, “I haven’t learned this yet, but I’ll keep practicing.” That’s a positive way to think. “I’ll never learn this, so why try?” is…
quests.hint: Compare “I’ll keep practicing” with “why try?”: which drains your energy?
quests.explanation: Positive thinking looks for what can go right. Negative thinking expects things to go wrong.
quests.funFact: In math, numbers above zero are called positive and numbers below zero are called negative.

quests.instruction: Seeing his neighbor was ill, Kiran left a card at her door, which was thoughtful. Blasting loud music under her window without thinking would be…
quests.hint: Think about who forgot to consider the neighbor’s feelings.
quests.explanation: Thoughtful people think about others and show care. Thoughtless people don’t stop to consider how others feel.
quests.funFact: “Thoughtful” can mean full of thought, or it can mean showing care for others.

quests.instruction: A wise person looks at dark clouds and takes an umbrella. Going to a picnic in a rainstorm with no coat would be…
quests.hint: Which choice shows good judgment?
quests.explanation: Wise choices come from good judgment. Foolish ones ignore signs that something may go wrong.
quests.funFact: Owls are a symbol of wisdom in many stories.

quests.instruction: Isha thanked her aunt for the birthday gift and wrote her a card, so she was grateful. Her cousin grumbled about the gift and never said thanks. He was…
quests.hint: One cousin wrote a card; the other grumbled and said nothing.
quests.explanation: Grateful means thankful for what you’ve received. Ungrateful means not showing any thanks.
quests.funFact: “Gratitude” comes from a Latin word meaning “pleasing” or “thankful”.

quests.instruction: The class expected a picnic and felt delighted. When rain cancelled it, they felt…
quests.hint: Imagine a picnic planned for weeks, then the rain arrives.
quests.explanation: Delighted means very pleased. Disappointed means sad that something hoped for didn’t happen.
quests.funFact: Farmers in many places plan their whole year around the rains.
